decisions.executionNote: Approach the gray nut with the right arm, gradually pitching down while maintaining elbow-up continuity; left remains parked.
Finish vertical gripper orientation and descend over the gray nut. Estimated nut center from calibrated head RGB; inspect alignment before grasp.
Close on the gray nut, lift vertically, then begin moving toward a central staging point. Retention must be checked visually.
Carry the retained gray nut to the center and lower for staging. Prepare the left arm in its own workspace, keeping separation.
Release the gray nut onto the center, lift and withdraw right. Bring left to a separated overhead pregrasp with vertical fingers.
Left approaches the staged gray nut vertically and closes; right moves further into its own workspace to clear the handoff.
Secure and lift the staged gray nut, then carry it above the matching gray screw on the left. Check retained nut and coaxial alignment next.
Refine gray nut alignment from RGB, lower onto its screw and begin a slow clockwise turn with slight axial advance.
Pause rotation and make a small lateral/axial alignment correction; the gray screw is not yet clearly centered in the nut opening.
Corrected tensor after zero execution. Lift clear of contact, refine lateral alignment, and lower the gray nut again.
Center the gray screw in the opening with a small correction, then turn clockwise slowly with a shallow axial advance.
Gray nut appears centered on the screw. Release and reset wrist rotation without lifting, then regrasp for another tightening stroke.
Gray nut fell beside the screw when released, so it was not threaded. Recover it from the table and correct the screw-axis estimate before retrying.
Lift the recovered gray nut clear, move to the screw axis estimated from its base rather than cap, and lower cautiously to insertion height.
The nut remained on the table. Regrasp at its updated visible center with fully open fingers, then test retention with a short vertical lift.
The gray nut is not stably centered between the fingers. Release it and lift slightly to obtain an unobscured settled pose before a corrected grasp.
Recenter on the settled gray nut and grasp slightly lower, then lift to test retention. Previous attempts appeared to catch only an edge.
Open and descend to inspect the gray nut at grasp height before closing; use wrist-image centering rather than assuming retention.
Correct the remaining lateral offset at grasp height, close fully, and perform a clear vertical retention test before any transfer.
Retention is now visible. Move the gray nut above the fixed screw axis and lower to a cautious pre-insertion height, without turning yet.
Use wrist RGB to remove the visible lateral screw-to-hole offset while retaining the nut, then lower only four millimeters to inspect engagement.
The screw is visible within the gray nut opening. Remove the small residual lateral offset and apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with shallow axial advance.
The gray screw cap is now centered within the nut. Open without lifting and reset the wrist for another tightening stroke, checking that the nut stays on the screw.
Gray nut remained on its screw after release. Regrasp and apply a clockwise tightening stroke, advancing only a few millimeters axially.
Release the engaged gray nut and unwind the open wrist for the next clockwise stroke, without lifting the nut off the screw.
Regrasp the still-engaged gray nut and add another controlled clockwise tightening stroke with minimal axial advance.
Open the gripper and reset its rotation while leaving the gray nut on the screw, preparing a final shallow tightening pass.
Apply the final shallow clockwise pass to the gray pair; it remains upright and engaged after the previous release.
Release the tightened gray pair, lift clear, and reset the left wrist while moving above the yellow nut for its center handoff.
Descend over the yellow nut with the left gripper upright and open; inspect centering at grasp height before closing.
Corrected a rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Grasp and lift the yellow nut, then carry it toward the center with the right arm stationary.
Place and release the retained yellow nut at the central staging point. Bring the right arm only to a separated pregrasp position.
Lift and withdraw the left arm before bringing the right above the staged yellow nut. Maintain lateral arm separation throughout the handoff.
Right grasps the staged yellow nut while left grasps the purple nut in its own workspace. Descend vertically and close before testing retention.
Lift both nuts, carry yellow above its matching screw, and bring purple near the central staging area. Keep both grippers closed and arms separated.
Lower the aligned yellow nut onto its screw. Stage and release purple centrally; its edge grasp looks less secure, so inspect the settled placement.
Correct the yellow screw-to-hole offset from wrist RGB before turning. Regrasp purple at its settled position for a better-centered handoff.
Turn the aligned yellow nut clockwise with a shallow axial advance. Move the now-centered purple nut onto the central staging point, retaining it until settled.
Yellow still shows a lateral cap offset, so pause turning and correct it before release. Leave purple on the center and withdraw the left arm.
The yellow screw is now centered in the opening. Seat it slightly lower, release without lifting, and begin resetting the open wrist to test engagement.
Yellow remains engaged after release. Reset and begin the next tightening pass while withdrawing the empty left arm toward its origin.
Complete the yellow tightening stroke, release and partially reset the wrist. Finish returning the empty left arm to its origin with gradual configuration-continuous motion.
Finish resetting the open right wrist, regrasp the engaged yellow nut, and begin the next shallow tightening stroke. Left stays at origin.
Complete the yellow tightening stroke, release while maintaining engagement, and partially unwind the open wrist for the final pass.
Finish the wrist reset and begin the final yellow tightening pass, keeping axial advance small and the left arm parked.
Complete the yellow tightening pass, release it, and lift the open right gripper clear while beginning to reset its wrist.
Move the open right gripper above the centrally staged purple nut and reset to its vertical grasp orientation; left remains at origin.
Grasp the staged purple nut at table height and lift vertically to verify secure retention before carrying it to its matching screw.
Carry the securely retained purple nut above its matching screw, then lower to a pre-insertion height for wrist-image alignment.
Remove the small visible purple screw-to-hole lateral offset and lower gradually to engagement height before applying rotation.
Refine the residual purple cap offset, seat slightly deeper, and apply a slow first clockwise tightening stroke while retaining the nut.
Purple contact deflected the wrist and exposed a lateral gap. Lift clear, restore an upright nut axis with offset compensation, and reapproach the screw without further turning.
Translate the purple nut toward the visibly right-offset screw cap, then lower four millimeters without rotation to check coaxial engagement.
Seat the now-centered purple nut slightly deeper, release without lifting, and reset the open wrist to verify that the nut remains engaged.
Purple nut fell beside its screw, so engagement was not achieved. Approach the settled nut with open fingers and inspect centering at grasp height before recovery.
The open jaw contacted the nearby purple screw during recovery. Lift clear and rotate the grasp direction to avoid the screw, then reapproach the nut.
Descend in the new collision-avoiding grasp direction, making a small wrist-image lateral correction. Inspect the nut at table grasp height before closing.
Center the purple nut between the rotated jaws, close fully, and lift vertically to verify retention clear of the adjacent screw.
The purple nut is visibly retained and centered. Bring it above the screw without changing the stable grasp, then lower to an inspection height.
Make a small lateral centering correction and lower slowly toward purple screw engagement, without twisting until the cap is clearly inside the opening.
The purple cap is still outside the opening. Lift off contact, correct the estimated longitudinal axis by eight millimeters, and reapproach without rotating.
The last correction increased the longitudinal gap. Lift clear, reverse that correction, and inspect the relative cap and hole position before further descent.
The longitudinal correction moved the cap toward the opening. Continue that visually confirmed direction with the nut retained, then lower only four millimeters and inspect.
Lower the purple nut slowly along the visually corrected axis without twisting. Check whether the screw cap enters fully before releasing or tightening.
Remove the remaining longitudinal purple cap offset in the visually confirmed direction, lifting slightly before the correction and reseating without rotation.
Purple is still not coaxially engaged and appears offset in the grasp. Lift clear and return toward a free staging area to obtain a centered upright grasp rather than forcing the threads.
Set the purple nut down in the clear central area and release it to settle upright, then lift the empty gripper for an unobscured centered regrasp.
Approach the settled upright purple nut at its newly observed center, descending with open fingers and checking wrist-image centering before regrasping.
Refine the lateral purple grasp center, close at a slightly deeper height, and test secure upright retention with a vertical lift.
The purple nut is retained but longitudinally off-center. Set it flat and recenter the grasp along that remaining offset before carrying it to the screw again.
The purple nut is now centered in the grasp. Lift and carry it above the matching screw using the updated head-camera axis estimate, keeping its orientation fixed.
Lower the centered upright purple nut straight down to insertion height, holding orientation and checking cap alignment before tightening.
The purple cap is left of the opening after descent. Lift clear, correct laterally toward the cap, and reseat gently without turning.
Refine both residual purple cap offsets with a small lifted correction, then lower five millimeters beyond the prior height. Keep the nut upright and do not twist until centered.
Remove the remaining right-side gap with a small lateral correction, lower two millimeters, and test engagement with only a short clockwise turn.
The cap crossed slightly to the opposite side of the hole. Apply a smaller compensating correction, seat gently, and continue a short clockwise engagement test.
